document.title: Host Control: let Deck Apps call linked computers through plugins
document.summary: Adds Host Control end to end: the `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` client and plugin registry, the Host Companion CLI with a read-only `system-stats` plugin, the native link listener and link store with a Shell Host Control screen, and a `host-control` example Deck App.
document.why: Máté asked for the three Host Control slices, shaped so later Deck Apps can send keys, read sensors and set controls, act like a Stream Deck, drive several machines on different OSes, and show a T3 Code dashboard ([session](source:s5)).

sources.title: Host Control slice A: wire contract and SDK client
sources.gist: JSON-over-HTTP contract, error codes, typed registry, `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control` client, shared fixtures.

sources.title: Host Control slice B: Host Companion CLI
sources.gist: Private companion package with `start` and `link`, config file, peer check, node:test suite.

sources.title: Host Control slice C: native link listener and Shell Host Control screen
sources.gist: Shared HTTP parsing, LAN address in platform, link listener and store, native getter, Shell entry and screen, C harness.

sources.label: PR #144
sources.gist: One PR for all three slices; plugins instead of a flat catalogue; several links; demo Deck App.

sources.label: T3 Code session · Oct 28
sources.gist: Implement all three issues; target use cases shape the design but are not built now; the backend extension model is left to the agent; add a demo Deck App.

lookFor: [#109](source:s1) asks for flat command names and an internal `defineHostCommands`. Every request instead names a `plugin`, and `defineHostPlugin` and `command` are public, because the [session](source:s5) left the extension model open and [PR #144](source:s4) chose plugins.

[#109](source:s1) and [#111](source:s3) name the getter `nativeGetHostControlUrl()` and one stored link in `host-control-link.json`. At head `nativeGetHostControlLinks()` returns a JSON array of up to 4 links in `host-control-links.json`, keyed by a new companion `id` in the link payload, so one Deck App can reach several machines ([session](source:s5)).
[#109](source:s1) asks for a new `test:sdk` script. At head the SDK host-control tests run under the existing `test:cli` glob; no source gives a reason.
[#110](source:s2) keeps one `vita` in the companion config. At head `vitas` is an array, since several Vitas can link one companion.
[#111](source:s3) describes a `Forget link` action. At head Cross on a linked computer row forgets that one link at once.
Credentials stay deferred, as ADR 0004 says, so the only plugins ([PR #144](source:s4)) read information; no acting command ships.

groups.title: Wire contract and SDK client
groups.why: Slice A: the contract every other piece speaks, and the client Deck Apps call ([#109](source:s1)).
groups.summary: `createHostClient` in `client.ts` turns a `defineHostPlugin` registry from `plugin.ts` into typed methods that POST the `protocol.ts` envelope and map every failure to a `HostResult`, checked against the shared fixtures.

groups.title: Host Companion CLI
groups.why: Slice B: the long-lived listener on the computer that performs the link and runs plugin commands ([#110](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `cli.ts` runs `start`, which serves `POST /command` from `server.ts` over the plugins `plugin.ts` loads, and `link`, which POSTs the link payload from `link.ts` and records the Vita in `config.ts`.

groups.title: system-stats plugin
groups.why: The first plugin proves the plugin split and gives the demo live gauges without acting on the computer ([PR #144](source:s4)).
groups.summary: `index.ts` is the registry a Deck App bundles and `companion.ts` implements its one `read` command with `node:os`, reading `vm_stat` on macOS.
lookFor: On macOS `memoryUsedPercent` counts free, inactive and speculative pages from `vm_stat` as available; elsewhere it uses `os.freemem()`, which reads `MemAvailable` on Linux.

groups.title: Shared native helpers moved out of upload and storage
groups.why: The link listener reuses Runtime Upload's request reading, the manifest's jimp parsing, and Deck App Storage's safe file replace, so [#111](source:s3) moves them where both callers reach them.
groups.summary: Upload's HTTP helpers move to `src/net/http.c`, its LAN address detection to `src/platform/lan_address_*`, jimp and JSON escaping to `src/core/json.c`, and Deck App Storage's replace-file logic to `vd_replace_file` in `src/core/util.c`.
lookFor: A Deck App Storage write that fails to move the old file aside now reports "Could not write Deck App Storage." instead of "Could not replace Deck App Storage."; the `.tmp` and `.bak` names stay the same, so a backup left by an older build is still recovered.
`http_read_request` always NUL-terminates the body it returns, so the link parser can hand it to jimp; Runtime Upload ignores the extra byte.

groups.title: Link listener, store and native getter
groups.why: Slice C: VitaDeck accepts a link only while asked, keeps it across restarts, and lets Deck Apps read it ([#111](source:s3)).
groups.summary: `listener.c` accepts one `POST /link` on 8798+, `link.c` validates it and stores up to 4 links through `vd_replace_file`, and `nativeGetHostControlLinks` in `jslib/host_control.c` hands the list to the SDK client.

groups.title: Shell Host Control entry and screen
groups.why: The user reads the link address and forgets links on the Vita ([#111](source:s3)).
groups.summary: A Host Control row after Upload opens `VD_SHELL_HOST_CONTROL`, which starts the listener, shows the address, status and linked computers, and stops the listener on a link, Circle, Start or shutdown.
lookFor: After a successful link the listener has stopped, so the screen swaps the `host-companion link` hint for "go Back and open Host Control again"; linking a second computer needs that round trip.

groups.title: host-control example Deck App
groups.why: The [session](source:s5) asked for a demo Deck App showcasing Host Control.
groups.summary: `App.tsx` polls `linkedHosts()` and each host's `systemStats.read`, lists the computers with live CPU, and shows the selected one's capabilities, gauges and an Echo round trip.
lookFor: After a `timeout` the demo polls that computer every 30 s instead of every second, because the native fetch keeps running up to its 30 s curl cap after the SDK gives up at 5 s.

groups.title: Glossary, ADR and checks
groups.why: Docs that the new design made inaccurate are fixed in place, and the companion tests join the `fast` tier ([#110](source:s2)).
groups.summary: `CONTEXT.md` adds the Host Control Plugin, Link Listener and Shell terms, ADR 0004 is rewritten for plugins and several links, `AGENTS.md` lists the new code, and `agent-check.sh fast` runs `test:host-companion`.

commits.subject: feat(examples): Host Control demo Deck App, docs, and agent-check
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Adds the host-control example, the Host Control glossary terms, rewrites
ADR 0004 for plugins and several links, adds the companion tests to the
fast tier, and makes system-stats read macOS memory like Activity Monitor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-control): Host Control Link listener, store, getter, and Shell screen
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Slice C of ADR 0004. VitaDeck keeps up to four Host Control Links in <data root>/host-control-links.json and exposes them to Deck Apps through nativeGetHostControlLinks. The Shell Host Control Screen starts a listener on 8798-8807 that accepts one POST /link, and Cross forgets a linked computer.

Upload's HTTP helpers move to src/net/http, LAN address detection to src/platform/lan_address_*, jimp's implementation and the JSON skip and escape helpers to src/core/json, and Deck App Storage's Vita-safe file replace to src/core/util so the link store reuses it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(host-companion): Host Companion CLI and system-stats plugin
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Adds @vitadeck/host-companion (start, link, implementHostPlugin, config) and
the first-party read-only @vitadeck/host-plugin-system-stats plugin, with
node:test coverage that replays the Host Control fixtures against the server.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(sdk): typecheck and lint the Host Control tests
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The SDK tsconfig did not include test/*.ts, so oxlint's type-aware rules saw
every host-control.test.ts value as an error type and pnpm lint failed. Include
the tests and fix the lint findings in the client and its tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
